en: Wearing an N95 mask during Mayon Volcano's ashfall protects your lungs from inhaling tiny, harmful volcanic glass particles.
When PAGASA raises Signal Number 3, you must evacuate coastal areas in provinces like Cebu to avoid deadly storm surges.
If you feel a strong earthquake near the coast of Surigao del Norte, immediately run to higher ground to escape a tsunami.
Avoid wading in floodwaters in Manila because rat urine in the water can transmit the serious bacterial disease leptospirosis through skin cuts.
Never eat shellfish from Samar during a red tide bloom because they accumulate paralytic shellfish poison that causes severe human illness.
Emptying unused tires in your Quezon City backyard prevents Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from breeding and spreading the dengue virus.
Apply sunscreen when visiting Boracay beach at noon because the tropical UV index reaches extreme levels that quickly burn skin.
Stay away from the steep mountain slopes of Benguet during heavy rain because saturated soil easily triggers deadly, fast-moving landslides.
If caught in a strong rip current while swimming in La Union, swim parallel to the shore instead of fighting back.
Wear closed shoes when walking in the grassy areas of Mount Makiling to protect your feet from venomous Philippine cobras.
Do not stand under a lone coconut tree in a Pampanga rice field during a thunderstorm because it attracts deadly lightning.
Drink plenty of water during the hot dry season in Tuguegarao to prevent heat stroke, as temperatures frequently exceed dangerous levels.
